threat: Compromise Faculty and Student Accounts to Commit Academic Fraud
threat_description: Adversaries target faculty and student accounts across learning management systems, productivity platforms, VPN infrastructure, and identity providers — using credential stuffing, phishing, and session hijacking to gain authenticated access. University accounts are high-value targets: a compromised faculty account grants access to gradebooks, unpublished course materials, student personal data, and institutional communication channels. A compromised student account enables grade manipulation, unauthorized exam access, and identity-based academic fraud. Compromised credentials are the dominant initial access vector in higher education incidents — the account is the attack surface.

motives.motive: Gain authenticated access to faculty accounts to manipulate grades, steal course materials, and access student personal data

components.name: Faculty Identity and Learning Platform Access
components.description: Identity provider and learning management infrastructure governing faculty authenticated access — Shibboleth, Okta, and Microsoft Entra ID federated to Instructure Canvas. IdP compromise yields simultaneous access to every connected service; Canvas compromise yields gradebooks, course materials, and student data.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-308: Use of Single-factor Authentication
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Single-factor authentication on the university IdP means one phished or infostealer-harvested password is sufficient to authenticate — with no second factor to interrupt the chain, that single credential grants access to every federated service the university operates, from the LMS to research storage.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: IdP administrative credentials stored without adequate protection allow attackers to gain control of the identity federation layer — issuing valid authentication tokens for any university user without knowing their passwords.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hard-coded service account credentials in IdP configuration files provide permanent authenticated access to the identity infrastructure — a discovered hard-coded credential grants the ability to create, modify, or impersonate any user account in the university directory.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: LMS and IdP roles are granted at course-catalog granularity rather than per-course, so an authenticated faculty account carries read and grade-write scope far wider than the courses that account actually teaches — the access-control decision cannot express the boundary the institution intends.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: LMS and IdP platforms authorize course-material and roster requests from the identifier supplied in the request without re-checking that the authenticated principal owns that course, so a compromised faculty account can reach any course's materials and student records by substituting the identifier.

components.name: Faculty Productivity and Remote Access Infrastructure
components.description: Productivity platform and VPN infrastructure providing faculty access to institutional resources and campus-internal systems — Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 combined with university VPN. Compromise provides both communication records and network-level access to campus-internal systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-308: Use of Single-factor Authentication
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Absence of MFA on faculty productivity platform accounts means a single phished password is the whole authentication decision — phishing-harvested credentials yield immediate access to email histories, shared drives, and communication records with no second factor to stop them.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: OAuth tokens for third-party integrations stored in application configurations without encryption provide delegated access to faculty email and documents without triggering MFA challenges.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hard-coded service account credentials in productivity platform integrations provide persistent access to shared institutional mailboxes and document repositories not subject to individual user password rotation policies.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: OAuth tokens and VPN configuration credentials stored without adequate protection in faculty device configurations allow attackers who compromise a single device to extract durable access tokens providing persistent access to productivity platforms and campus networks beyond the initial device compromise.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hard-coded service account credentials in VPN and productivity platform integrations provide network access paths and data access that cannot be revoked through normal credential reset procedures, persisting even after a suspected compromise event.

motives.motive: Compromise student accounts to manipulate academic records, access financial aid systems, and commit identity fraud

components.name: Student Account Management Systems
components.description: Authentication and account management infrastructure governing student access to university digital services — student portals, registration systems, financial aid platforms, and learning management systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies in student account systems allow attackers to brute-force or credential-stuff student accounts at scale — universities with large student populations present millions of potential targets with historically low password hygiene, making bulk account compromise operationally straightforward.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Credentials harvested through phishing or infostealer malware are replayed directly against student portals — the authentication mechanism cannot distinguish a captured-and-replayed credential from a live one, so stolen credentials yield immediate access to academic records and financial aid data.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Student portal roles are scoped at application level rather than per-record, so any authenticated student account carries read scope across student data far beyond the account holder's own record — the permission model cannot express a per-student boundary.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Student portal systems authorize record access from the client-supplied student identifier without verifying that the authenticated session owns that record, allowing a single compromised account to enumerate and access the academic and financial records of the entire student body.

threat: Exfiltrate Student and Faculty Records from University Systems
threat_description: Adversaries target the centralized repositories of personal, financial, and academic data that universities maintain on students and faculty — exploiting weak access controls, unencrypted storage, and SQL injection vulnerabilities to extract records at scale. Universities hold some of the most comprehensive personal data profiles of any sector: Social Security numbers, financial aid records, health information, immigration status, and years of behavioral and academic history for populations of tens of thousands. The 2026 Global Cyber Risk Outlook for Higher Education recorded a 73% rise in higher education data breaches over the twelve months to October 2025 against the preceding twelve months — the open network architecture and federated data access that enable academic collaboration create the same vulnerabilities that enable mass data exfiltration.

motives.motive: Extract bulk student and faculty personal records for identity theft, financial fraud, and dark web resale

components.name: Student Information System Platform Access
components.description: Authentication and authorization layer governing access to student information systems — Ellucian Banner, Oracle PeopleSoft, Workday HCM. The identity controls that determine who can reach the full student and faculty record database.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies on data management system administrative accounts allow attackers to brute-force or credential-stuff privileged access — a single compromised administrator account provides access to the full student and faculty record database without requiring further privilege escalation.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Credentials obtained through phishing or infostealer malware are replayed against university data platforms — with no binding between the credential and the session that established it, captured credentials grant direct access to platforms holding personal records at scale.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Misconfigured data management platform APIs expose student and faculty personal records to unauthenticated or low-privilege requests — publicly accessible student directories or poorly scoped API responses can expose PII at scale without requiring authentication bypass.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Data repository roles are defined at system level rather than per-record-class, so an authenticated user with a limited operational role carries read scope across student and faculty records far beyond that role's purpose — the access-control model has no granularity to express the intended limit.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Data management platforms authorize record retrieval from the user-supplied record identifier without verifying that the authenticated principal is entitled to that record, allowing attackers to enumerate and extract student and faculty records sequentially.

components.name: Student and Faculty Data Repositories
components.description: The underlying data storage, application logic, and web interface layers of university data management systems — the components through which student and faculty records are stored, processed, and surfaced to users and integrations.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Student and faculty personal records stored without encryption are immediately usable by any attacker who gains storage access — unencrypted Social Security numbers, financial aid records, and health information require no additional decryption step after exfiltration.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SQL injection vulnerabilities in student information system query interfaces allow attackers to bypass application-layer access controls and extract the full student and faculty database through the application's own database connection — a single injection point yields the complete institutional data set.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Deserialization vulnerabilities in university data management software allow attackers to inject manipulated objects that execute arbitrary code within the data platform, establishing persistent access to student and faculty records beyond the initial exploitation window.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSRF vulnerabilities in student information system web services allow attackers to pivot from internet-facing portals to internal data repositories containing student and faculty records not directly accessible from external network interfaces.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Code injection vulnerabilities in university web portals allow attackers to introduce malicious scripts executing in the server context, accessing student and faculty data stores with the application's own database permissions.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities in university authentication portals allow attackers to craft phishing links on the university's own domain that redirect students and faculty to credential-harvesting sites — the trusted institutional domain increases campaign success rates.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unrestricted file upload vulnerabilities in student and faculty portals allow attackers to introduce malicious executables executing in the web server context, establishing persistent access to data management systems containing the full institutional record population.

threat: Falsify Student Academic Records for Fraudulent Advancement
threat_description: Adversaries exploit SQL injection vulnerabilities, weak authorization controls, and insufficient audit mechanisms in student information systems and registrar platforms to alter grades, modify transcripts, change enrollment status, and manipulate financial aid eligibility. Academic record falsification enables degree fraud, scholarship retention through falsified GPA maintenance, and professional credential fraud when falsified transcripts are submitted to employers or graduate programs. The harm extends beyond the individual: institutions that cannot guarantee the integrity of their academic records face accreditation risk and legal liability when falsified credentials surface in employment or licensing contexts.

motives.motive: Manipulate student grade and transcript records to obtain fraudulent academic credentials or financial aid

components.name: Ellucian Banner (SIS)
components.description: Student information system managing academic records, enrollment, registration, and financial aid for hundreds of universities globally — the authoritative system of record for student academic history and degree progress.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SQL injection vulnerabilities in Banner SIS query interfaces allow attackers to bypass application-layer authorization and directly modify grade records, enrollment status, and transcript data in the underlying database — bypassing the audit controls built into the application layer that would otherwise log the change.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Banner authorizes record reads and writes from the student identifier carried in the request without re-checking that the authenticated principal is entitled to that record, so an authenticated user can manipulate the identifier to reach and modify academic records belonging to other students.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Insufficient access controls on Banner SIS data access interfaces expose sensitive student academic records — including disciplinary history, financial aid eligibility, and academic standing — to users whose role does not justify that access.

components.name: Oracle PeopleSoft Campus Solutions
components.description: Enterprise student information and campus management platform managing academic records, advising, financial aid, and degree audit functions across large university systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SQL injection in PeopleSoft Campus Solutions data access components allows unauthorized modification of the academic record database — grade changes made directly at the database layer bypass the application's audit trail, leaving no record of the manipulation in standard reporting.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: PeopleSoft authorizes administrative record-modification functions from the user-supplied employee or student identifier rather than from the authenticated session's own entitlements, allowing an attacker to reach record-modification functions restricted to registrar staff.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Misconfigured PeopleSoft data access controls expose academic standing, financial aid eligibility, and disciplinary records to users with insufficient authorization — intelligence about record structure that informs more targeted falsification attacks.

components.name: University Registrar Portal
components.description: Web-based registrar interface through which students, advisors, and administrative staff access and manage enrollment, grade submission, and official transcript generation.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SQL injection in registrar portal data submission forms allows attackers to inject malicious queries modifying grade and enrollment records directly in the underlying database, bypassing the application workflow controls that require faculty approval for grade changes.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: The registrar portal authorizes grade-submission and transcript functions from manipulated student or course identifiers without verifying the authenticated principal's entitlement, allowing any authenticated student to reach grade submission and transcript generation.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Insufficient access controls on registrar portal data queries expose other students' academic records — providing the information needed to make falsified records consistent with institutional formatting and grading patterns.

components.name: Financial Aid Database
components.description: Database systems managing student financial aid eligibility, award calculations, disbursement records, and academic progress requirements — systems whose data integrity determines whether students receive or retain financial assistance.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SQL injection vulnerabilities in financial aid database interfaces allow attackers to alter academic progress records that determine aid eligibility — falsifying the GPA and credit completion records that trigger Satisfactory Academic Progress reviews and financial aid suspension.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Financial aid systems authorize eligibility-record access and modification from the supplied student identifier without verifying entitlement, allowing students to reach and alter their own or their peers' aid eligibility records directly.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Improper access controls on financial aid systems expose award calculation logic, eligibility thresholds, and academic progress requirements — intelligence that enables precisely targeted record falsification to maintain aid eligibility while evading detection.

threat: Steal University Research Data and Intellectual Property
threat_description: Adversaries target university cloud infrastructure, research lab servers, high-performance computing clusters, and intellectual property repositories to exfiltrate government-funded research data, proprietary scientific findings, pre-publication results, and patentable innovations. US academic institutions spent $117.7 billion on research and development in FY2024 according to the NSF Higher Education Research and Development survey — representing decades of accumulated intellectual value stored on infrastructure with access controls calibrated for academic openness rather than competitive protection. Nation-state actors and corporate espionage operations treat university research networks as lower-resistance alternatives to corporate R&D targets. In a joint fact sheet issued 30 June 2025, CISA, the FBI, DC3 and the NSA warned that Iranian-affiliated cyber actors may target vulnerable US networks and entities of interest, with organizations holding Israeli research and defense relationships at elevated risk.

motives.motive: Exfiltrate government-funded research data and pre-publication findings for competitive or national intelligence advantage

components.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS) Research Environment
components.description: Cloud computing infrastructure hosting university research workloads, datasets, and computational models — S3 buckets, EC2 research clusters, RDS databases, and SageMaker environments containing research data and intermediate results.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: AWS IAM policies and S3 bucket ACLs on the research environment are assigned more permissively than intended — publicly readable buckets and overly broad cross-account grants make research datasets and computational results reachable without any authorization decision being made against the requester.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Insufficiently scoped AWS resource policies expose research data and experimental results to authenticated users beyond the research team — overly permissive cross-account access or publicly readable storage configurations disclose research findings before publication.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: AWS access keys stored in source code repositories, Jupyter notebooks, or shared configuration files allow attackers to authenticate directly to research cloud environments and exfiltrate datasets without triggering identity-based detection.

components.name: University Research Lab Server
components.description: On-premises research computing infrastructure hosting experimental data, proprietary datasets, and research code — systems managed by individual research groups with heterogeneous security postures and limited central IT oversight.

sub_components.name: Faculty-managed lab server shares and accounts

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Research lab servers managed by individual faculty carry permissions set for convenience rather than least privilege — open network shares, world-readable directories and default service accounts leave research data reachable by any account on the campus network.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Research lab servers running unpatched services expose sensitive research data through known vulnerability exploitation — UpGuard's university security-rating research published in 2023 detected software with known exploited vulnerabilities at 48% of all universities and 70% of the top 500.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Research lab server credentials shared informally among team members and stored in unprotected configuration files allow any attacker who obtains a single credential to access the full research data store.

components.name: High-Performance Computing (HPC) Cluster
components.description: Shared computational infrastructure supporting large-scale research simulations and data analysis — Slurm-managed clusters and NSF-funded supercomputing allocations. Compromise provides both data access and significant compute resources.

sub_components.name: HPC scheduler accounts and shared scratch storage

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: HPC job submission and scratch storage permissions are assigned at cluster scope rather than per-allocation, so any account on the cluster can read another research group's job output directories and intermediate datasets.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: HPC environments where research data is written to shared scratch filesystems without access restrictions expose intermediate computational results and training datasets to any cluster user.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSH keys for HPC cluster access shared among research team members or stored without passphrase protection allow any party who obtains the key material to authenticate as legitimate researchers and exfiltrate project data.

components.name: Intellectual Property Repository
components.description: Repositories holding patent applications, proprietary research methodologies, licensing agreements, and pre-publication research — technology transfer office systems and secure research data vaults with concentrated IP value.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: IP repository object permissions are assigned at repository scope rather than per-document, leaving unpublished patent applications and pre-publication findings readable by users well beyond the research team and technology transfer office.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Misconfigured IP repository access policies expose pre-publication research findings and patent applications — disclosure of pending patent applications before filing can invalidate the patent and eliminate the institution's commercial rights to the research.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: IP repository access credentials with insufficient protection allow attackers to authenticate and exfiltrate the full contents of patent application databases and proprietary research archives — the long-term commercial value makes this a priority target for nation-state and corporate espionage operations.

threat_description: Adversaries deploy ransomware across university file servers, email systems, backup infrastructure, faculty workstations, and student network drives — encrypting operational data and demanding payment for restoration. Comparitech recorded 251 ransomware attacks claimed against educational institutions worldwide in 2025, with attacks in the first quarter of 2025 running 69% above the same quarter of 2024. Comparitech's Education Ransomware Roundup of July 2026 attributed a 275% rise in education-sector attacks in the first half of 2026 against the second half of 2025 largely to The Gentlemen ransomware operation, 80% of whose education victims were colleges and universities. The operational dependency is the leverage: a university that cannot access grades, transcripts, or financial information cannot function academically or administratively. The Community College of Beaver County closed its campus after discovering encrypted data on 9 March 2026, leaving students and staff unable to reach grades, transcripts and billing systems; in-person classes did not fully resume until 30 March, and the Interlock group claimed the attack.

motives.motive: Encrypt university operational data to halt academic and administrative functions and extort ransom payment

components.name: University File Server
components.description: Centralized file storage infrastructure holding faculty research files, administrative documents, course materials, and institutional records — the primary ransomware target given its broad accessibility across the university network.

sub_components.name: Campus file share access and permissions

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak or phished credentials for file server access allow ransomware operators to authenticate to shared storage infrastructure and deploy encryption payloads across all accessible network shares — university file servers with broad authenticated access provide ransomware maximum coverage from a single credential compromise.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: File server share permissions granted broadly across the campus network give any compromised account write access to shared storage, which is exactly the reach ransomware needs to encrypt institutional data from a single initial foothold.

components.name: University Backup System
components.description: Backup infrastructure storing recovery copies of university operational data. Ransomware operators specifically target backup systems to eliminate recovery options and maximize extortion leverage before deploying encryption on production systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Backup repository permissions are assigned to the same accounts and network scope as production systems, so the credentials that let ransomware operators reach production also let them encrypt or delete the backup copies that would otherwise make recovery possible.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Backup system administrative credentials shared with general IT staff or stored in accessible configuration files allow ransomware operators to authenticate to backup management interfaces and corrupt or delete backup repositories before deploying production encryption.

components.name: Faculty Workstations
components.description: Faculty endpoint devices holding locally stored research data, course materials, and cached credentials — initial ransomware targets providing both local encryption coverage and network credential harvesting for lateral movement to servers.

sub_components.name: Faculty endpoint credential stores and local privilege

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Credentials cached on faculty workstations — browser-saved passwords, VPN configurations — allow ransomware to harvest network credentials and move laterally to file servers, email systems, and research storage before triggering encryption.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Faculty workstations run with local administrator rights assigned as the default rather than by exception, letting ransomware delivered through phishing install persistence mechanisms and disable endpoint protection without any privilege escalation step.

components.name: On-Premise Email and Student Network Storage
components.description: On-premise email servers and student shared network drives — systems whose encryption disrupts day-to-day academic operations and increases ransomware leverage by shutting down both communications and collaborative work.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Email server and student network drive service account credentials allow ransomware operators who obtain them to encrypt both communication records and student collaborative work simultaneously — compounding operational disruption beyond file server encryption alone.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Email server and student network storage share the same permission scope, so ransomware that enters through a student network drive inherits write access to administrative mail stores rather than being contained to student data.

threat: Defraud Students Through Tuition and Fee Payment System Manipulation
threat_description: Adversaries exploit CSRF vulnerabilities, cleartext transmission, and weak cryptographic implementations in university payment gateways and financial databases to intercept tuition payments, redirect funds, and falsify payment records. University payment systems process high-value transactions — tuition and fee payments range from thousands to tens of thousands of dollars per student — and typically integrate international payment processors that introduce additional cross-border jurisdiction complexity. Manipulation of payment records can simultaneously defraud students, create false enrollment records, and expose the institution to significant regulatory and contractual liability.

motives.motive: Intercept, redirect, or falsify tuition and fee payments for direct financial gain

components.name: Flywire (Payment Gateway)
components.description: International student payment platform processing tuition and fee payments from students in over 240 countries — a primary payment channel for international student tuition at universities globally.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Absence of CSRF protections on payment initiation endpoints allows attackers to forge payment requests redirecting tuition funds to attacker-controlled accounts — a student authenticated to the payment portal can be tricked into submitting a forged payment order through a malicious link.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Cleartext transmission of payment session data between university portals and the payment API exposes payment credentials and transaction parameters to interception — enabling manipulation of payment destination or amount before settlement.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak cryptographic implementations in payment API signature verification allow attackers to forge payment authorization tokens — submitting modified payment amounts or destination accounts that pass signature validation due to algorithm weaknesses.

components.name: TransferMate (Payment Processor)
components.description: Cross-border payment processing platform used by universities for international student fee collection — a specialist platform whose integration with institutional financial systems creates additional data transmission attack surface.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Missing CSRF protections on payment processor integration endpoints allow forged requests to modify payment routing or initiate unauthorized transaction reversals — redirecting international tuition payments mid-transfer.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Cleartext transmission of payment processing credentials between university systems and the payment processor exposes API authentication tokens, enabling attackers to authenticate to the payment processor and initiate unauthorized transactions.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak cryptographic protections on payment processing API responses allow interception and decryption of transaction details — exposing student payment credentials and enabling replay attacks against payment authorization flows.

components.name: University Financial Database
components.description: Core financial data infrastructure recording tuition payments, fee assessments, scholarship disbursements, and account balances — the authoritative record of student financial standing with the institution.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Missing CSRF protections on financial database management interfaces allow forged requests to alter payment records, waive outstanding balances, or create false payment confirmations — enabling falsification of financial standing records without actual payment.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Cleartext internal communication between financial database tiers exposes payment records and account balance data to interception — enabling manipulation of financial records in transit between application and database layers.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak encryption on stored financial records allows attackers who gain storage access to decrypt and modify payment histories — creating false payment records without triggering integrity validation.

components.name: University Billing Portal
components.description: Student-facing billing interface through which students view account balances, initiate payments, and access payment history — the web application layer connecting students to the financial database and payment processors.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: CSRF vulnerabilities in billing portal payment submission forms allow attackers to trigger unauthorized payment actions against authenticated student sessions — forging payment redirection requests that execute with the student's billing portal authentication.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Cleartext transmission of billing portal session data exposes payment authentication tokens to interception, allowing replay of valid payment sessions with modified transaction parameters.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Broken cryptographic implementations in billing portal session management allow attackers to forge valid session tokens, gaining authenticated access to payment functions without the student's credentials.

threat: Distribute Malware Across University Networks to Harvest Credentials
threat_description: Adversaries exploit the open, collaborative nature of university networks — where file sharing, software installation, and cross-institutional data exchange are normal academic activities — to distribute malware across campus infrastructure. University networks typically span thousands of endpoints with heterogeneous operating systems, inconsistent patch levels, and BYOD policies that introduce unmanaged devices. Malware distributed across campus networks harvests credentials, establishes persistent access for ongoing espionage, and creates infrastructure for external attacks. The open architecture that enables academic collaboration becomes the propagation path for malware that reaches research systems, administrative databases, and the personal devices of tens of thousands of students and faculty.

motives.motive: Deploy credential-harvesting malware across campus networks to enable account takeover and sustained institutional access

components.name: Campus Authentication and Endpoint Infrastructure
components.description: Authentication systems, endpoint devices, and network credential stores across the campus environment — the layer where malware harvests credentials and establishes lateral movement paths to higher-value systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies allow malware operators who harvest credentials through keyloggers or network capture to crack or reuse collected passwords across multiple university systems — university environments with thousands of accounts and inconsistent MFA enforcement make bulk credential harvesting operationally effective.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Malware on university workstations and remote access systems captures authentication material and replays it against other campus systems — the authentication mechanism accepts a replayed credential or hash as equivalent to a live logon, establishing persistent access without ever cracking a password.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Cleartext credential transmission and exposed network security logs allow malware to harvest authentication data from network traffic — legacy university systems that do not enforce encrypted authentication provide broad credential exposure opportunities.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Campus file-sharing permissions are assigned broadly across a flat network, giving any account write access to shares that every other account reads — the permission assignment itself is what lets malware propagate from one compromised account to the wider campus population.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: File-sharing platform write permissions are granted at share scope rather than per-directory, so any authenticated account can place executable content into directories that the whole institution reads, with no granularity to separate publishing rights from read access.

components.name: University Web Applications and Network Services
components.description: University-hosted web portals, academic applications, and network services — the delivery and propagation channels through which malware reaches campus endpoints via trusted institutional infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Deserialization vulnerabilities in university academic applications provide initial code execution for malware deployment — exploiting these vulnerabilities requires no user interaction and provides immediate code execution in the application server context.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSRF vulnerabilities in university research and academic platforms allow malware command-and-control communications to be routed through legitimate university servers, making malware traffic indistinguishable from normal institutional web activity.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Code injection vulnerabilities in university web portals allow malware to be delivered through legitimate university domains — users who trust the institution's domain are more likely to execute delivered payloads.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unrestricted file upload in university portals allows malware to be hosted on legitimate university infrastructure and distributed to campus users through trusted channels — institutional hosting bypasses domain-reputation-based security controls.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities in university authentication systems allow malware delivery links to appear to originate from trusted university domains — students and faculty who recognize the university URL are more likely to follow links that redirect to malware download sites.

threat: Gain Unauthorized Physical Access to Campus Facilities
threat_description: Adversaries exploit weaknesses in campus access control systems, electronic lock infrastructure, and physical security management software to gain unauthorized entry to campus buildings, research laboratories, data centers, and sensitive facilities. University campuses present a unique physical security challenge: they must remain accessible to large populations of students, faculty, and the public, while protecting research laboratories containing valuable equipment, data centers, student residential areas, and facilities housing government-sensitive research. Unauthorized physical access enables equipment theft, research data exfiltration through direct media access, laboratory sabotage, and compromise of student safety. IT-OT convergence means a network compromise can grant remote control of physical access infrastructure without any physical presence on campus.

motives.motive: Bypass electronic access controls to enter restricted campus facilities for theft, espionage, or sabotage

components.name: Access Control Management Platform
components.description: Software management layer administering campus access control policies, credential issuance, and security monitoring — Lenel, Software House, CCURE. The remote attack surface for access control system compromise.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies on access control management system interfaces allow attackers to gain administrative access to the platform controlling physical entry to all campus facilities — a single compromised administrator account enables remote unlocking of any electronically controlled campus door.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Access control management interfaces expose credential-issuance and door-configuration functions that perform no authentication check of their own, relying on network position instead — reaching the interface is sufficient to create credentials and alter door schedules.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Exposed access control system logs reveal facility occupancy schedules, security response times, and movement patterns of high-value targets — intelligence enabling physical surveillance and planned unauthorized access.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Electronic lock management roles distinguish only between 'user' and 'administrator', with no granularity between monitoring a door and reconfiguring it, so any campus account that reaches the platform carries far more physical-access authority than its holder's job requires.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Access control systems authorize entry decisions from the credential identifier presented at the reader without server-side validation that the credential was issued to the bearer, so cloned or spoofed keycard data is accepted as legitimate.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Deserialization vulnerabilities in physical security management software allow remote code execution within the access control management system — providing persistent control over facility access without requiring physical interaction with door hardware.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSRF vulnerabilities in campus security web platforms allow attackers to reach internal access control management systems from internet-facing interfaces — pivoting from the public network to the physical security management layer controlling campus door access.

components.name: Physical Access Control Hardware and Interfaces
components.description: Keycard readers, electronic lock controllers, door hardware interfaces, and associated firmware — the physical layer where access credentials are presented and validated, and where hardware-level attacks achieve physical entry.

sub_components.name: Keycard reader and lock controller management interfaces

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Code injection in campus security system web interfaces allows attackers to execute arbitrary code within the security management platform, enabling remote modification of access control policies and door lock states.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirects in security system management portals are used to phish campus security administrators — redirecting them to credential-harvesting sites that capture security management credentials enabling subsequent physical access control modification.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unrestricted file upload in university security system portals allows attackers to deploy malicious firmware to connected access control devices, modifying door lock behavior to permit unauthorized entry while displaying normal status to security monitoring systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak input validation in keycard terminal firmware or access control management interfaces allows injection of malformed commands that override access control decisions — causing doors to grant entry to invalid credentials or disable alarm triggers for unauthorized access events.

threat: Deny Students and Faculty Access to Digital Campus Services
threat_description: Adversaries flood university authentication systems, course delivery platforms, library services, and student portal infrastructure with malicious traffic or exploitative requests that exhaust processing capacity and deny legitimate access. Higher education institutions face an average of 4,388 cyberattacks per week — more than double the global average across all sectors. Universities are particularly vulnerable: exam periods, enrollment windows, and financial aid deadlines create concentrated periods of peak demand that are also high-leverage attack windows. Denying access to digital services during final examinations or registration periods creates maximum academic disruption from minimum attack investment.

motives.motive: Exhaust digital service resources to deny students and faculty access during critical academic periods

components.name: University Authentication and Session Management
components.description: Identity provider, SSO, and session management infrastructure governing access to all digital campus services — the availability bottleneck whose failure cascades to every dependent platform.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies allow attackers to compromise accounts at scale and use them to amplify availability attacks — compromised legitimate accounts bypass rate limiting controls designed to detect unauthenticated flooding.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: University portals apply no limit on authentication attempt volume, so attackers can drive the authentication tier to resource exhaustion and lock legitimate students and faculty out of their accounts through repeated failed logons during peak academic periods.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Exposure of authentication system configuration allows attackers to identify and exploit specific availability bottlenecks — targeting authentication infrastructure components whose failure cascades to all dependent services.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Service infrastructure roles are coarse enough that an account provisioned for routine operations also carries authority to disable accounts and take services offline, giving an attacker who reaches any administrative role the ability to block legitimate access.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Session and service management functions are authorized from supplied session or service identifiers without verifying the caller's entitlement, letting an attacker manipulate other users' sessions and disable access for the wider campus population.

components.name: Campus Digital Service Applications
components.description: LMS, library systems, student portals, and administrative platforms — the application layer where availability attacks manifest as service denial for students and faculty during critical academic periods.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Deserialization vulnerabilities allow attackers to crash service processes through malformed payloads — triggering repeated service restarts that effectively deny availability without requiring sustained flooding.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSRF vulnerabilities allow attackers to target internal infrastructure components that other services depend on — disrupting core internal services cascades availability failures to all dependent student-facing platforms.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Code injection in university authentication platforms allows attackers to introduce malicious scripts degrading service performance or corrupting session handling — causing authentication failures for all users attempting to access campus digital services.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unrestricted file upload in university service portals allows deployment of scripts consuming server resources or corrupting service state — causing cascading availability failures across digital service infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities allow attackers to redirect users away from legitimate services — combined with phishing, these redirects can suppress legitimate authentication attempts during high-demand periods.

threat: Hijack University Computing Resources for Cryptomining and Illicit Operations
threat_description: Adversaries exploit weak authentication and authorization controls on university computing infrastructure — research servers, HPC clusters, cloud computing allocations, and GPU workstations — to deploy cryptomining software, conduct AI model training at institutional expense, or establish infrastructure for external attacks. University computing environments are disproportionately targeted for resource theft: HPC clusters provide GPU compute equivalent to thousands of commercial nodes, research cloud allocations carry significant dollar value, and the open computing culture creates tolerance for unfamiliar workloads. Cryptomining generates direct financial harm through electricity costs and cloud charges, degrades research computing performance, and can result in loss of government computing allocations when abuse is detected by funding agencies.

motives.motive: Gain unauthorized access to university computing infrastructure to conduct cryptomining and illicit compute operations at institutional expense

components.name: Research Computing Access and Authorization
components.description: Authentication and authorization layer governing access to HPC clusters, cloud computing allocations, and GPU research workstations — the controls that determine who can submit workloads and consume compute resources.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies on research server accounts allow attackers to brute-force or credential-stuff access to computing infrastructure — a single compromised research account on an HPC cluster provides access to the full compute allocation associated with that account.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Research computing job submission endpoints accept work without authenticating the submitter, relying on network position or a shared cluster account, so an attacker who reaches the endpoint can queue cryptomining workloads that appear as legitimate research jobs.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Exposure of research computing usage logs and infrastructure configuration allows attackers to identify high-value targets — GPU nodes with underutilized capacity, cloud allocations with remaining budget, and research servers with sustained uptime suitable for long-running mining operations.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Compute allocation roles are granted at project scope with no granularity between consuming a quota and altering it, so any account on the platform can escalate to compute resources well beyond its allocation.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Compute resource allocation is authorized from the supplied allocation identifier without verifying the requester owns it, letting an adversary claim GPU quotas and HPC allocations belonging to other research groups.

components.name: University Computing Management and Job Submission Infrastructure
components.description: Job scheduling platforms, cloud management consoles, and resource monitoring systems — the administrative interfaces through which computing workloads are submitted, managed, and tracked across university infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Deserialization vulnerabilities in university computing management software allow attackers to inject malicious workload configurations deploying cryptomining processes across managed compute infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSRF vulnerabilities in university cloud management systems allow attackers to reach internal compute allocation APIs — enabling submission of mining workloads to institutional cloud environments through internal network paths bypassing external API authentication.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Code injection in university cloud platform management interfaces allows attackers to introduce malicious scripts deploying mining workloads using the platform's own job submission infrastructure — appearing as legitimate compute jobs in resource usage reports.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unrestricted file upload in university computing portals allows attackers to introduce mining software disguised as research code — deployed through legitimate job submission workflows providing compute access without triggering malware detection.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities in university cloud management portals redirect administrators to credential-harvesting sites — captured administrative credentials provide access to compute resource management enabling large-scale illicit workload deployment.

threat: Compromise Campus Building Systems to Create Physical Safety Hazards
threat_description: Adversaries gain unauthorized access to campus building management and automation systems — HVAC, elevators, fire suppression, lighting, and emergency systems — and manipulate operational parameters to create unsafe conditions for students, faculty, and staff. Modern university buildings integrate IP-connected building management systems sharing network infrastructure with administrative and academic IT environments. The convergence of IT and OT on university campuses means a network compromise beginning in an academic system can escalate to physical control of building infrastructure — HVAC manipulation creating hazardous laboratory conditions, elevator control trapping occupants, or fire suppression interference endangering lives during an actual emergency. The attacker does not need to enter the building to endanger those inside it.

motives.motive: Manipulate campus building automation to create physical hazards for students and staff or render facilities unusable

components.name: Building Management System Platform
components.description: Software management layer administering campus HVAC, elevator, fire suppression, and environmental control systems — Honeywell, Siemens, Johnson Controls, Schneider Electric. The remote management interface through which building systems are configured and controlled.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies on BMS management interfaces allow attackers to gain unauthorized access to building control systems — a compromised BMS administrator account provides remote control over HVAC, elevator, and fire suppression systems across all managed campus facilities.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: BMS control functions are reachable without an authentication check of their own — IT-OT convergence puts building control endpoints on routable campus networks where reaching the interface is treated as sufficient authority to actuate HVAC, elevator and fire suppression systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Exposed BMS configuration data reveals building system architecture, control interface endpoints, and safety system parameters — intelligence enabling targeted attacks against specific safety-critical building functions.

sub_components.name: BMS control authorization and safety interlocks

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: BMS roles do not separate facilities monitoring from operational control, so an account provisioned to read building status also carries authority to change setpoints and safety parameters — read access escalates to physical actuation with no further step.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: BMS control interfaces authorize setpoint and interlock changes from the supplied device or zone identifier without verifying the operator's entitlement to that equipment, allowing safety interlocks and operating limits to be overridden.

components.name: Building Automation Control and OT Network
components.description: The operational technology layer executing building control commands — PLCs, SCADA interfaces, BACnet/Modbus network segments, and the web and application interfaces connected to campus IT networks that provide the IT-OT convergence path.

sub_components.name: BACnet and Modbus controller software and gateways

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Deserialization vulnerabilities in building management software allow attackers to inject malformed data corrupting automation control logic — altering programmed behavior of building systems to create physical hazards without requiring ongoing attacker interaction.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SSRF vulnerabilities in campus building automation web interfaces allow attackers to reach internal BMS control systems from internet-facing portals — using the web server's internal network access to send commands to building control systems not directly exposed externally.

sub_components.name: BMS operator interfaces on the IT-OT boundary

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Code injection in BMS web portals allows attackers to introduce malicious scripts altering building control parameters — modifying HVAC setpoints, disabling alarm triggers, or corrupting elevator control logic through the management interface.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unrestricted file upload in BMS management portals allows attackers to deploy malicious scripts or firmware introducing persistent control logic modifications that create ongoing safety hazards.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities in BMS management portals redirect building administrators to credential-harvesting sites — captured BMS credentials provide remote access to building system controls that can be manipulated to create physical safety hazards.

threat: Defraud Federal Financial Aid Programs Using AI-Generated Ghost Student Identities
threat_description: Organized crime rings use AI tools to generate synthetic student identities — blending stolen personal information with fabricated details — and enroll ghost students at colleges and universities to trigger federal financial aid disbursements diverted to attacker-controlled accounts. AI chatbots complete coursework to keep ghost students enrolled long enough to receive aid refunds. The Department of Education reported preventing over $1 billion in federal student aid fraud since January 2025, and on 24 July 2026 FinCEN issued alert FIN-2026-Alert004, in consultation with the Department of Education Office of Inspector General and the FBI, warning that fraud rings are targeting the Federal Student Aid program that disburses more than $120 billion a year to roughly 13 million students. California's community college system identified nearly one in three applicants in 2024 as fraudulent. The institution bears the reputational, regulatory, and financial consequences when fraudulent aid flows through its enrollment systems.

motives.motive: Enroll AI-generated synthetic identities as students to fraudulently obtain and divert federal financial aid disbursements

components.name: University Admissions and Enrollment System
components.description: Online admissions portals, application processing systems, and enrollment management platforms through which prospective students establish enrollment status — the entry point for ghost student fraud where synthetic identities are submitted as legitimate applications.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak identity verification during online enrollment allows AI-generated synthetic identities to complete the application process without presenting verifiable credentials — absence of live identity verification or government ID validation at enrollment enables ghost students to establish enrollment status using fabricated identity data.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Insufficient validation of submitted identity documents allows forged transcripts, fabricated Social Security numbers, and AI-generated supporting documents to pass admission review — admissions systems relying on document appearance rather than cryptographic verification cannot distinguish AI-generated documents from authentic ones.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Failure to verify the authenticity of submitted identity documents with issuing authorities allows AI-fabricated government IDs and high school transcripts to satisfy enrollment requirements — ghost students pass identity verification relying on document appearance rather than external validation.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Enrollment system interfaces expose workflow configuration, verification thresholds and application status detail to low-privilege and unauthenticated requests, giving organized fraud operations the reconnaissance needed to identify the minimum proof an application must carry to pass review.

components.name: Financial Aid Disbursement System
components.description: Federal financial aid processing and disbursement infrastructure — FAFSA verification systems, institutional Student Aid Management platforms, and refund disbursement mechanisms. The endpoint where ghost student fraud converts enrollment into fraudulent financial transfers.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Aid eligibility roles are scoped to the disbursement system as a whole rather than to verified enrollment status, so ghost students who clear initial enrollment carry the same disbursement entitlement as verified students, with no granularity linking aid to enrollment legitimacy.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Financial aid systems authorize disbursement record access and bank-detail changes from the supplied student ID number without additional verification of the requester, so a fabricated but well-formed student ID is sufficient to redirect aid payments.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak authentication on financial aid disbursement account management allows fraudsters to modify bank account details associated with ghost student financial aid records — redirecting aid refunds to attacker-controlled accounts without triggering identity verification required for disbursement account changes.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Financial aid disbursement accepts enrollment and identity attestations from upstream admissions without independently verifying them against the issuing authority, so AI-fabricated identity and enrollment evidence that cleared admissions is treated as verified fact at the point money is released.

threat: Conduct State-Sponsored Espionage Against University Research Programs
threat_description: Nation-state threat actors conduct sustained, targeted intrusion campaigns against universities conducting government-funded research — particularly in defense, semiconductor, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and energy sectors. A joint CISA, FBI, DC3 and NSA fact sheet of 30 June 2025 warned that Iranian-affiliated cyber actors may target vulnerable US networks and entities of interest, singling out organizations with Israeli research and defense ties and poorly secured internet-connected devices. Unlike opportunistic attackers, state-sponsored actors invest in long dwell periods, spearphishing campaigns specifically targeting named researchers, and exploitation of research collaboration infrastructure. Universities are targeted precisely because their security posture is calibrated for academic openness rather than classified information protection — the same environment enabling international research collaboration provides the access surface for sustained espionage.

motives.motive: Exfiltrate government-funded defense and technology research through sustained long-dwell intrusion campaigns

components.name: University Research Collaboration Infrastructure
components.description: Platforms supporting cross-institutional and international research collaboration — Confluence research wikis, SharePoint research portals, GitHub research repositories, and video conferencing systems used for sensitive research discussions.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-308: Use of Single-factor Authentication
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Research collaboration platforms authenticate on a single factor, so a spearphished researcher password is the entire authentication decision — state-sponsored actors obtain long-dwell access to collaboration spaces without needing to defeat any second factor.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Insufficiently protected collaboration platform credentials allow state-sponsored actors to extract and maintain persistent access — API tokens and OAuth credentials stored in research codebases provide durable access persisting through researcher account password changes.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Collaboration space permissions are granted at workspace scope rather than per-project, so visiting researchers and external collaborators admitted for one project carry read access across sensitive research well beyond it.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-346: Origin Validation Error
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Research collaboration platforms that do not validate the origin or integrity of shared files allow state-sponsored actors to introduce malware through legitimate research sharing channels — a compromised external collaborator becomes a trusted delivery vector for research espionage tools.

components.name: Secure Research Computing Environment
components.description: Isolated or controlled-access computing environments for sensitive government-funded research — ITAR-controlled research networks, CUI (Controlled Unclassified Information) data systems, and secure enclaves for export-controlled research data.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: The boundary between standard university networks and the controlled research computing environment enforces no authentication step of its own, so an actor who compromises a standard campus account traverses into the controlled environment without presenting further credentials.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak password policies on controlled research environment access allow state-sponsored actors to conduct credential attacks against researchers with access to classified or export-controlled data — a single compromised researcher account can exfiltrate the entire controlled dataset without triggering perimeter controls.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Cleartext data transmission within research computing environments allows state-sponsored actors with network access to passively intercept research data transfers without triggering access control violations.

threat: Deceive University Staff Through AI-Generated Impersonation to Commit Payroll Fraud
threat_description: Adversaries use AI tools to automate reconnaissance against universities — scraping public faculty directories, organizational charts, and LinkedIn profiles — then generate highly convincing spearphishing emails, voice messages, and text communications impersonating university executives, HR administrators, and IT support staff. Recent campaigns specifically targeted university HR and payroll teams, impersonating benefits officers and payroll administrators to trick employees into entering credentials on fake portals — then using those credentials to redirect payroll deposits to attacker-controlled accounts. AI-written content and cloned institutional branding make these attacks indistinguishable from legitimate communications at scale. Compromised credentials remain the dominant route into higher education environments, and AI-powered social engineering has become the leading way those credentials are obtained.

motives.motive: Deceive HR and payroll staff into disclosing credentials or authorizing fraudulent payroll changes through AI-generated impersonation

components.name: University HR and Payroll Systems
components.description: Human resources and payroll management platforms processing faculty and staff compensation, direct deposit configurations, and benefits enrollment — Workday HCM, ADP Workforce Now, Banner HR. The target of payroll redirection attacks enabled by staff credential theft.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-294: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payroll credentials harvested through AI-generated phishing are replayed directly against payroll administration functions — the system accepts a captured credential as equivalent to a live logon, so the phished password immediately becomes payroll administration access.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payroll system credentials cached in staff browsers allow attackers who compromise a staff device through phishing to extract and reuse authentication tokens — accessing payroll functions without triggering re-authentication that would reveal the attacker.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payroll direct deposit changes are authorized by a single role with no separation between initiating and approving the change, so one compromised HR account carries end-to-end authority to redirect employee compensation.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payroll change workflows completable without out-of-band verification are defeated by credential phishing — an attacker who obtains credentials through AI-generated spearphishing can complete payroll changes through the normal authenticated workflow without triggering controls designed to detect unauthorized changes.

components.name: University Staff Email and Communication Systems
components.description: Email, messaging, and voice communication infrastructure through which AI-generated impersonation attacks are delivered — the channel through which convincing fake executive or IT communications reach HR and payroll staff.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-346: Origin Validation Error
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Email systems without DMARC, DKIM, and SPF enforcement allow AI-generated phishing emails to spoof university executive and IT department addresses — the impersonated sender address passes visual inspection by HR staff because the domain appears authentic.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: University IT support workflows that reset credentials based on information available in staff directories allow vishing attacks using AI-cloned voices to obtain credential resets — providing direct payroll system access without requiring email phishing.
